abstract: This project is the proof-of-concept game development of a digital trading card game Battle of Talingchan which is transformed from a physical card to online multiplayer game experience. This game is developed using Unity engine, the game features a 1v1 matchmaking system that is powered by Photon to ensure the real time interactions between players. The final product is deployed online via itch.io. The gameplay is according to the rule sets of the original physical card game along with Thai themed characters which include in all cards. This game structured included four distinct phases which are Draw phase, Main phase, Battle phase and End phase. Detailed project specifications and guidance were provided by TOYLAXY (LION HOUSE CO., LTD.).

abstract: FiscAI is a personal finance management application that is designed to simplify and make it convenient to track expenses. Some of the individuals find it hard and time-consuming to write down their daily costs manually particularly where they have a lot of receipts. FiscAI is meant to address this issue by applying Large Language Models (LLMs) with Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to scan and extract receipts into information. The system can identify important details such as the store name, purchased items, and tax information, which helps reduce the need for manual data entry. The application is developed using a modern full-stack approach, where the frontend is built with React and the backend is powered by Deno. This structure allows the system to run efficiently while maintaining a responsive user experience. One of the key features of FiscAI is its support for multiple languages, including English and Thai, which makes the application more accessible to different users. In addition, the system also provides real-time financial forecasting, allowing users to better understand their spending habits and plan their finances more effectively. FiscAI combines AI-based automation with traditional data management features to create a practical and user-friendly tool for managing personal finances.

abstract: The Rangoon QR Ordering System is a web-based digital solution developed for Rangoon Food House, a Burmese restaurant that serves authentic Myanmar cuisine. The system aims to improve the restaurant ordering process by utilizing QR code technology, allowing customers to scan a QR code at their table to access the menu, place orders, and interact with the system directly through their mobile devices. The system provides two main interfaces: a customer interface and an admin interface. Customers can browse menu items, view prices in Thai Baht, customize orders, and choose between dine-in or takeaway options. In addition, the system includes features such as order history and a waiter call function, which sends a notification sound to staff when assistance is requested. On the admin side, the system enables staff to manage menu items, monitor and update orders in real-time, and view order history with filtering options. It also includes a dashboard that provides insights into daily sales, total revenue, and popular menu items to support better decision-making. The system is developed using modern web technologies, including React.js for the frontend, Laravel (PHP) for the backend, and MySQL for the database. By implementing this system, Rangoon Food House can enhance service efficiency, reduce waiting time, minimize human errors, and improve the overall customer dining experience.

abstract: This project is about the development of Jewelry Shop Management System, which is intended for the operation and management of the daily activities of a jewelry business. The system assists in managing significant business information such as customers, products, invoices, purchases, vendors, promotions, and material sources. The organization and storage of such information using the system are expected to improve data accuracy, efficiency, and transparency for the operation and management of the business. Using the Jewelry Shop Management System, users are able to manage products, inventory, customers' purchases, and vendors' buyback. Additionally, the system is also used for price management using gold price history and promotion discounts. The structure of the system is based on a relational database design that connects different entities such as products, customers, invoices, and vendors. Using the Jewelry Shop Management System, the operation and management of a jewelry business are expected to be more effective and efficient for the owners and managers. In particular, the system is expected to help the owners and managers monitor products, sales, and customers in a more systematic and reliable manner. In essence, the project is about the potential benefits and advantages of using information systems and database technologies for the operation and management of the jewelry retail industry.

canonical_title: Using PCG to Explore Data Augmentation Strategies for Robust Classifiers
advisor: Asst. Prof. Dr. Dobri Atanassov Batovski
abstract: This senior project examines data augmentation as a design variable for robustness-oriented image classification rather than as a routine preprocessing step. The study focuses on handwritten equation recognition from whiteboard images collected in a low-resource classroom-style setting. A balanced dataset of 240 images was organized into four classes — linear equations, quadratic equations, rational expressions, and inequalities — and split into fixed training, validation, and test partitions. Two convolutional neural network models were trained under matched conditions, including the same dataset split, model architecture, and training schedule. The only controlled difference was the augmentation strategy. The baseline model used a generic library-style augmentation workflow, while the proposed condition used a scenario-aware procedural content generation (PCG) pipeline designed to simulate classroom capture effects such as lighting variation, blur, noise, perspective change, and partial occlusion. Evaluation was conducted on both a standard held-out test set and a shared shifted test set. The generic model achieved 67.5% accuracy on the standard test and 65.0% on the shifted test, while the PCG model achieved 80.0% and 72.5%, respectively. The corresponding confusion matrices show that both models recognized linear equations reliably, but the PCG pipeline reduced some of the most severe class confusions, especially under shift, for quadratic and rational forms. At the same time, the generic model exhibited a smaller clean-to-shift drop, indicating a trade-off between absolute accuracy and relative stability. Taken together, the results show that augmentation design materially changes error behavior and robustness outcomes. For robustness-oriented computer vision, scenario-aware augmentation can therefore be a practical and interpretable strategy when deployment conditions differ from the clean training distribution. The proposed system is designed for smart classroom environments, where automated recognition of handwritten educational content can support lecture capture and digital learning tools.
